property_summary: The function sudicideAnyone should revert when called by an account that is not the smartfix_owner
c.sudicideAnyone() must revert when called by any address other than c.smartfix_owner().
c.sudicideAnyone() must always revert when called from any address.
c.sudicideAnyone() must always revert when called by any address.
c.sudicideAnyone() must revert when called by an account other than smartfix_owner.
The function sudicideAnyone only succeeds for the smartfix_owner
sudicideAnyone succeeds for the owner and fails for others
A call to sudicideAnyone reverts if and only if the caller is not smartfix_owner.
A call to sudicideAnyone reverts if and only if the caller is not smartfix_owner.
A call to sudicideAnyone reverts if and only if the caller is not smartfix_owner.
The function sudicideAnyone must succeed (not revert) when called by smartfix_owner; the buggy version reverts for everyone including the owner.
After a call to sudicideAnyone, the contract's code size becomes zero (it is destroyed) for the correct version, while the buggy version remains alive with non-zero code size.
For any caller, calling sudicideAnyone() on C never reverts if the caller is the owner; the buggy version always reverts, so a call from the owner does not revert on C but reverts on M.
For any caller, calling sudicideAnyone() on C reverts if and only if the caller is not the owner; the buggy version always reverts, so a call from a non-owner succeeds on C but also reverts on M.
For any caller who is the smartfix_owner, calling sudicideAnyone() must not revert; the buggy version always reverts, so a call from the owner reverts on M but succeeds on C.
After a call to sudicideAnyone by the owner, the contract's code size (or balance of the original caller) should become zero in the reference but it stays non-zero in the mutant.

After a successful sudicideAnyone call by the owner, the contract should be destroyed so that any subsequent attempt to call sudicideAnyone again will revert in the reference (no code at address), while in the mutant the contract survives and calling sudicideAnyone again would succeed (not revert).

After a successful call to sudicideAnyone by the owner, the reference contract is destroyed (its code size becomes zero), whereas the mutant survives with non-zero code size; the property asserts that a subsequent staticcall to the contract returns empty data and succeeds, which holds for the destroyed reference but fails for the surviving mutant.

After a successful sudicideAnyone call by the owner, any subsequent external call to the contract must revert because the contract is destroyed; the buggy contract survives, so a subsequent call succeeds.

Immediately after a successful sudicideAnyone call by the owner, the owner's address field smartfix_owner becomes the zero address in the reference (due to contract destruction) but remains the original owner in the mutant.
After selfdestruct, all remaining Ether in the contract must be sent to msg.sender (the caller), but the buggy version incorrectly sends it to smartfix_owner instead.

After a successful selfdestruct via sudicideAnyone, the contract code must be emptied (code size becomes 0), and the call's origin (tx.origin) must receive the Ether; the buggy version incorrectly sends Ether to smartfix_owner, which may differ from tx.origin, violating the code-emptied invariant when the call is routed through a relay.
For any msg.sender that satisfies smartfix_owner == msg.sender, a call to sudicideAnyone() must transfer all remaining Ether to msg.sender; the buggy version sends it to smartfix_owner instead.
